codes.label: Code completion
codes.definition: Copilot generates or completes statements, lines, functions, classes, or other source code from the surrounding code context.

codes.label: Comment-to-code
codes.definition: Copilot implements functionality from a natural-language comment or pseudocode description.

codes.label: Algorithms and data processing
codes.definition: Copilot implements algorithms, calculations, collection operations, data transformations, or query logic.

codes.label: Integration and configuration
codes.definition: Copilot generates configuration, API integration, authentication, database, deployment, or framework-specific code.

codes.label: Documentation and explanation
codes.definition: Copilot produces comments, documentation, summaries, or explanations of code.

codes.label: Testing and correction
codes.definition: Copilot generates tests, debugging changes, fixes, or automated code corrections.

codes.label: Non-code artifacts
codes.definition: Copilot generates text-like artifacts such as diagrams, translations, or commit messages.

codes.label: Implement functionality
codes.definition: Copilot is used to build a requested feature or solve a programming task.

codes.label: Troubleshoot code
codes.definition: Copilot is used to diagnose an error, repair code, or propose a workaround.

codes.label: Learn and understand
codes.definition: Copilot is used to learn a language or API, understand generated code, or obtain an explanation.

codes.label: Accelerate repetitive work
codes.definition: Copilot is used to reduce effort on boilerplate, repetitive edits, or routine coding.

codes.label: Evaluate AI capability
codes.definition: Copilot is deliberately tested or compared to assess its ability, trustworthiness, or usefulness.

codes.label: Discover code or APIs
codes.definition: Copilot is used as an alternative to documentation, search, IntelliSense, or manual API discovery.

codes.label: Create supporting artifacts
codes.definition: Copilot is used to create documentation, tests, diagrams, translations, or other development artifacts.

codes.label: Saves time and effort
codes.definition: Copilot reduces implementation time, typing, searching, or repetitive manual work.

codes.label: Produces working solutions
codes.definition: Copilot supplies code that solves the stated problem or works after little modification.

codes.label: Context-aware assistance
codes.definition: Copilot infers useful completions from comments, nearby code, naming patterns, or coding style.

codes.label: Broad environment support
codes.definition: Copilot is valued for assisting across multiple languages, editors, frameworks, or task types.

codes.label: Supports learning
codes.definition: Copilot helps users, especially novices, discover approaches or understand unfamiliar programming concepts.

codes.label: Generates substantial code
codes.definition: Copilot can produce complete functions or multi-step implementations from short prompts.

codes.label: Incorrect or fabricated output
codes.definition: Copilot suggests code, APIs, imports, properties, or syntax that is wrong, nonexistent, incomplete, or unsuitable.

codes.label: Requires verification
codes.definition: Generated code is opaque or untrusted and must be understood, tested, corrected, or checked against documentation.

codes.label: Intrusive suggestions
codes.definition: Automatic suggestions are distracting, verbose, noisy, or interfere with the user's editing flow.

codes.label: IDE and extension conflicts
codes.definition: Copilot conflicts with editor behavior, IntelliSense, snippets, extensions, keyboard shortcuts, or other completions.

codes.label: Authentication and access
codes.definition: Installation, authorization, account selection, subscription access, or repeated sign-in prevents Copilot use.

codes.label: Network and certificate barriers
codes.definition: VPNs, proxies, firewalls, DNS, SSL inspection, or self-signed certificates disrupt Copilot connectivity.

codes.label: Compatibility limitations
codes.definition: Copilot is unavailable or unreliable for a particular editor, platform, architecture, language, file type, or software version.

codes.label: Reliability and performance
codes.definition: Copilot crashes, hangs, disappears, stops suggesting, consumes resources, or breaks after an update.

codes.label: Limited user control
codes.definition: Users cannot adequately control triggering, acceptance granularity, formatting, scope, or other completion behavior.

codes.label: Privacy and security risk
codes.definition: Use raises concerns about sending proprietary code, exposing secrets, telemetry, retention, or generated credentials.

codes.label: Limited context or output range
codes.definition: Copilot lacks sufficient project context, returns only short suggestions, or provides too few useful alternatives.

codes.label: Poor documentation and discoverability
codes.definition: Copilot settings, commands, behavior, or generated APIs are undocumented or difficult to discover.

codes.label: Cost and restricted availability
codes.definition: Payment, trials, waitlists, licensing, or limited preview access restricts adoption.

codes.label: Partial acceptance
codes.definition: Users expect controls to accept a suggestion by word, line, or selected portion rather than all or nothing.

codes.label: On-demand and scoped activation
codes.definition: Users expect manual triggering and selective enablement by project, language, context, or content type.

codes.label: Style and format configuration
codes.definition: Users expect configurable quotes, line endings, completion length, and adherence to project conventions.

codes.label: Broader platform support
codes.definition: Users expect Copilot to support additional IDEs, operating systems, architectures, languages, and notebook environments.

codes.label: Robust enterprise connectivity
codes.definition: Users expect reliable authentication and first-class support for proxies, VPNs, corporate certificates, and restricted networks.

codes.label: Seamless IDE coexistence
codes.definition: Users expect Copilot to coexist with IntelliSense, extensions, snippets, keybindings, and native editing behavior without conflicts.

codes.label: Project context and personalization
codes.definition: Users expect multi-file project awareness, organizational knowledge, customization, or fine-tuning.

codes.label: Higher output quality
codes.definition: Users expect suggestions that compile, use current APIs, satisfy requirements, and require less correction.

codes.label: Extension and UI APIs
codes.definition: Users expect APIs or hooks for integrating, capturing, rendering, or extending Copilot-style completions.

codes.label: Privacy controls
codes.definition: Users expect local, self-hosted, opt-in, or organizational controls over source-code transmission and retention.

codes.label: Richer suggestion navigation
codes.definition: Users expect reliable multiline completions, multiple alternatives, and convenient next/previous navigation.

codes.label: Expanded assistant functions
codes.definition: Users expect integrated chat, explanation, documentation, testing, diagramming, or correction capabilities.
